threats.name: Adversarial Machine Learning
threats.description: Supplying deceptive inputs (e.g., physically altered stop signs, adversarial noise patches) to cause vehicle perception systems to misclassify objects or respond inappropriately to road conditions.

elapsedTime.rationale: Generating and validating physical-world adversarial examples is highly time-consuming.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires advanced data science and machine learning expertise to exploit neural network gradients.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: White-box attacks require access to the training weights; black-box requires extensive API querying.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Line-of-sight placement of a physical adversarial patch or projector near the target's sensor path is an easily obtainable window (roadside, parking).

equipment.rationale: Requires heavy GPU compute for model training and evasion testing.

threats.notes: Same underlying Auto-ISAC ATM technique (ATM-T0005) as T.20.1 (Affect Vehicle Function), modeled independently here under the Manipulate Environment tactic with its own capability and feasibility profile.

threats.name: Analog Sensor Attacks
threats.description: Disrupting availability or spoofing inputs of analog sensors (e.g., shining a laser into a Lidar receiver, transmitting ultrasonic noise) without directly altering the vehicle's mechanics.

elapsedTime.rationale: Shining a laser or emitting ultrasonic noise at a sensor produces an immediate effect.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Basic operation of a laser pointer or ultrasonic emitter requires no specialized expertise.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Basic physics applies to all OEMs identically (lasers blind cameras).

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Line-of-sight proximity to the target sensor during operation is an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: Commodity lasers or ultrasonic transducers are sufficient.

threats.notes: Same underlying Auto-ISAC ATM technique (ATM-T0004) as T.20.2 (Affect Vehicle Function), modeled independently here under the Manipulate Environment tactic with its own capability and feasibility profile.

threats.name: Downgrade to Insecure Protocols
threats.description: Jamming modern secure frequencies (e.g., 4G/5G, WPA3) to force the vehicle's wireless interfaces to failover to older, vulnerable legacy protocols (e.g., 2G GSM, WEP) to facilitate eavesdropping.

elapsedTime.rationale: Jamming the modern-protocol frequency until the target's modem fails over to a legacy protocol takes minutes to hours of sustained transmission, with reconnaissance to confirm fallback behavior.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate RF engineering skill to isolate and suppress the specific modern-band frequency without full-spectrum jamming.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Cellular/Wi-Fi failover behavior to legacy protocols (2G, WEP) is publicly documented standard behavior.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Physical proximity to the vehicle for the duration of the jamming is an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: Requires SDRs capable of precise frequency isolation and suppression.

threats.name: Jamming or Denial of Service
threats.description: Emitting excessive RF noise to block Wi-Fi, cellular, GPS, or key fobs, preventing the vehicle from communicating with external entities.

elapsedTime.rationale: Jamming effect is immediate upon transmission.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Jammers require no expertise to operate.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: RF jamming exploits shared-spectrum physics and requires no vehicle- or OEM-specific knowledge.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Physical proximity to the vehicle during the jamming window is an easily obtainable condition.

equipment.rationale: Commercial jammers are inexpensive and easily acquired.

threats.name: Manipulate Communication
threats.description: Intercepting and altering network traffic between the vehicle and a remote server/mobile device (MitM) by exploiting insecure or improperly implemented TLS/encryption schemas.

elapsedTime.rationale: Establishing a MITM position and exploiting a weak TLS configuration takes days.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate networking and cryptography skill to identify and exploit weak or improperly implemented TLS.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: TLS is a public protocol; only the target's specific misconfiguration (weak cipher, missing pinning) needs discovery.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: An on-path position via rogue AP or compromised network is readily obtainable.

equipment.rationale: Commodity MITM proxy tooling is sufficient.

threats.name: Relay Communications
threats.description: Relaying RF communications to make a trusted device appear physically closer to the vehicle than it is, bypassing distance-bound security assumptions (e.g., Key Fob PKES relay theft).

elapsedTime.rationale: Attack takes seconds once the equipment is in range.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Operating a turnkey RF relay device requires no specialized expertise.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Tools are turnkey and OEM-agnostic for vulnerable LF/RF systems.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Proximity to both the key fob and the vehicle simultaneously is an easily obtainable condition in common scenarios (driveway, parking lot).

equipment.rationale: Commodity RF relay/amplifier boxes are commercially available and sufficient.

threats.name: Rogue Cellular Base Station
threats.description: Setting up a malicious cellular eNodeB/femtocell (IMSI Catcher) to trick the vehicle's telematics unit into connecting, allowing eavesdropping or manipulation of backend communications.

elapsedTime.rationale: Configuring and broadcasting a convincing rogue base station to attract the target TCU takes days of setup and testing.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate cellular-protocol expertise to configure a convincing eNodeB/femtocell.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Cellular network-attach procedures are public 3GPP standards; only the target modem's specific attach preferences need observation.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: The vehicle will attempt attach whenever the rogue station is broadcasting nearby, an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: IMSI catchers and cellular SDRs are highly specialized hardware.

threats.name: Rogue Wi-Fi Access Point
threats.description: Deploying unauthorized Wi-Fi access points to intercept connections from the vehicle's infotainment system or diagnostic interfaces to execute network-based attacks.

elapsedTime.rationale: Deploying a rogue AP and waiting for auto-connect is fast.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Commoditized tools (e.g., Wi-Fi Pineapple) automate this entirely.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Wi-Fi association behavior is a fully public 802.11 standard; no OEM-specific knowledge is required.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: The target will probe/connect whenever the rogue AP broadcasts a known or open SSID nearby, an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: Commodity Wi-Fi Pineapple-class hardware is sufficient.

threats.name: Aftermarket, Customer, or Dealer Equipment
threats.description: Adversaries may use aftermarket, customer, or dealer equipment (e.g., paired smartphones, fleet management dongles, dealer diagnostic tools) as an initial access point into the vehicle.

elapsedTime.rationale: Compromising a paired phone app or dongle firmware takes days of analysis.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Exploiting a known vulnerability in commodity aftermarket dongle firmware requires only proficient-level skill.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Aftermarket dongle/app implementations are commercially available for analysis; not OEM-confidential.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires the dongle to be physically paired/plugged in or the phone app installed, a moderately constrained condition.

equipment.rationale: Standard mobile/firmware analysis tools suffice.

threats.name: Browser Compromise
threats.description: A browser compromise is when an adversary gains access to a system through a user visiting a website. The user's web browser is targeted for exploitation (e.g., WebKit/V8 engine flaws).

elapsedTime.rationale: Developing reliable zero-click or 1-click browser exploits with sandbox escapes takes months of dedicated effort.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires elite-level proficiency in memory corruption, JIT compilation flaws, and sandbox escapes.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Browser engine internals (WebKit/V8) are open-source and publicly documented; only the specific unpatched bug is undisclosed.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: The IVI browser is reachable whenever the user visits an attacker-controlled or compromised page, an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: Purely software exploit delivery; no special equipment required.

threats.name: Exploit Via Radio Interface
threats.description: The vehicle may be targeted for exploitation through its interface to cellular networks or other radio interfaces via baseband vulnerabilities or malicious SMS parsing.

elapsedTime.rationale: Developing baseband exploits requires substantial time and reverse engineering of proprietary stacks.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Baseband exploitation requires advanced proficiency in real-time operating systems and low-level radio firmware.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires reverse-engineered knowledge of the specific baseband firmware's proprietary stack, not publicly documented.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: The cellular/radio interface is always reachable whenever the vehicle has network coverage, with no timing constraint.

equipment.rationale: Requires specialized SDRs and cellular network simulation equipment (eNodeB).

threats.name: Exploit Via Removable Media
threats.description: Adversaries may gain initial access by copying malware to removable media (e.g., USB drive) and taking advantage of automatic parsing of files (e.g., media parsers) when inserted.

elapsedTime.rationale: Crafting malware that triggers on auto-parsing of a media file format takes days of testing against the specific parser.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate exploit-development skill targeting a specific media-parsing library.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Common media-parser vulnerabilities are researched against publicly available parsing libraries.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires physical access to the vehicle cabin to insert the removable media.

equipment.rationale: A standard USB drive is sufficient; no special equipment is required.

threats.name: Malicious App
threats.description: Malicious applications could be used by adversaries to gain a presence on a vehicle. This includes evading vetting in official stores or distributing via third-party repositories.

elapsedTime.rationale: Evading app-store vetting or compromising the distribution channel to get a malicious app installed takes months of preparation.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate mobile-app development and evasion expertise to bypass vetting processes.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires non-public knowledge of the specific vetting process's detection gaps or signing-key compromise.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: App stores/distribution channels are continuously open for submission attempts.

equipment.rationale: Standard app-development tooling is sufficient.

threats.name: Phishing
threats.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim credentials or deploy malicious code. This relies heavily on social engineering the vehicle owner or fleet manager.

elapsedTime.rationale: Phishing campaigns can be spun up very quickly using automated tools.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Crafting a convincing phishing message requires only basic social-engineering skill.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Generic phishing techniques require no OEM-specific or vehicle-specific knowledge.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Phishing campaigns can be launched at any time and repeated, an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: Standard email/SMS sending tools are sufficient.

threats.name: Physical Modification
threats.description: The adversary can make physical modifications to the vehicle's ECUs, wiring harnesses, or swap out legitimate ECUs for malicious ones to gain initial access.

elapsedTime.rationale: Fabricating or modifying an ECU/harness and integrating it undetected takes months.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate hardware-engineering skill to modify or replace an ECU convincingly.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: General ECU form factors and harness connectors are discoverable via public repair documentation.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires extended, unobserved physical access to the vehicle (workshop, overnight) for the modification.

equipment.rationale: Standard automotive electronics tools (soldering iron, connector kits) are sufficient.

threats.notes: Requires physical possession of the target hardware (see T.06.6, Physical ECU / Vehicle Access) - modeled as an independent Root Attack Step rather than a formal capability prerequisite, since no capability in this taxonomy exclusively represents physical possession without being reachable through this catalog's dense software-privilege capability graph as well.

threats.name: Supply Chain Compromise
threats.description: Adversaries may manipulate products or product delivery mechanisms prior to receipt by a final consumer (e.g., compromised OEM software repositories or vendor hardware).

elapsedTime.rationale: Compromising a vendor's software repository or hardware manufacturing line before it reaches the OEM takes months.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate supply-chain/software-security expertise to insert and conceal a compromise.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires non-public knowledge of the specific vendor's build/delivery pipeline.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires compromising a vendor network long before the vehicle reaches the consumer.

equipment.rationale: Software-level repository compromise requires no special equipment.

threats.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
threats.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters (e.g., Python, Javascript, bash) to execute arbitrary commands, scripts, or binaries within the vehicle's environment.

elapsedTime.rationale: Discovering and abusing an accessible script interpreter takes days of exploration once initial access exists.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate scripting and systems knowledge to abuse an interpreter for unauthorized commands.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Common interpreters (Python, bash, JavaScript) are publicly documented general-purpose tools.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires that a script interpreter be reachable from the attacker's foothold, a moderately constrained condition depending on hardening.

equipment.rationale: No special equipment beyond the existing execution access is required.

threats.name: Native API

threats.name: Standard Cryptographic Protocol
threats.description: Adversaries employ a known encryption algorithm embedded in their malware to conceal exfiltration traffic, bypassing network-level DLP (Data Loss Prevention) or IDS.

elapsedTime.rationale: Embedding a standard encryption library for exfiltration traffic is fast, automated payload generation.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Embedding standard crypto libraries is basic, but designing traffic that convincingly evades DLP/IDS requires intermediate skill.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: AES/TLS are fully public cryptographic standards requiring no confidential knowledge to implement.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Once execution access exists, encrypted exfiltration channels can be established at will.

equipment.rationale: Standard open-source crypto libraries are sufficient.

threats.notes: Same underlying Auto-ISAC ATM technique (ATM-T0066) as T.18.6 (Command and Control), modeled independently here under the Exfiltration tactic with its own capability and feasibility profile.

threats.name: Removable Media
threats.description: Adversaries may attempt to exfiltrate data via a physical medium, such as a USB drive connected to the infotainment system.

elapsedTime.rationale: Copying collected data to a connected USB drive is fast.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires only basic file-system familiarity.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: USB mass-storage handling is a fully public, standard OS feature requiring no OEM-specific knowledge.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Physical access to the cabin USB ports is required.

equipment.rationale: A standard USB drive is sufficient.

threats.name: Physical Access
threats.description: Physical access via a JTAG / debug / serial interface could be used to exfiltrate data -- for example, extracting private keys or firmware via memory remanence/cold boot attacks.

elapsedTime.rationale: Hardware extraction takes significant time for setup, probing, and dumping.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires advanced hardware hacking and reverse engineering.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires knowledge of the specific chip's memory layout and remanence characteristics, not publicly documented.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires extended, unobserved physical possession of the removed board for probing and dumping.

equipment.rationale: Requires logic analyzers, decapsulation tools, or environmental cooling gear.

threats.notes: Requires physical possession of the target hardware (see T.06.6, Physical ECU / Vehicle Access) - modeled as an independent Root Attack Step rather than a formal capability prerequisite, since no capability in this taxonomy exclusively represents physical possession without being reachable through this catalog's dense software-privilege capability graph as well.

threats.name: Affect Vehicle Function
threats.description: The adversary is trying to affect vehicle functions and systems, such as propulsion control, airbag deployment, audio, and displays. This is the ultimate impact tactic in the automotive domain.

elapsedTime.rationale: Umbrella rating derived from this category's own children: the lowest-bar (easiest-for-attacker) elapsed time value found among them is ET1, from T.20.2 (Analog Sensor Attacks) - the most accessible instantiation of this abstract tactic along this dimension.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Umbrella rating derived from this category's own children: the lowest-bar (easiest-for-attacker) specialist expertise value found among them is SE1, from T.20.2 (Analog Sensor Attacks) - the most accessible instantiation of this abstract tactic along this dimension.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Umbrella rating derived from this category's own children: the lowest-bar (easiest-for-attacker) knowledge of the item/component value found among them is KoIC0, from T.20.2 (Analog Sensor Attacks) - the most accessible instantiation of this abstract tactic along this dimension.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Umbrella rating derived from this category's own children: the lowest-bar (easiest-for-attacker) window of opportunity value found among them is WoO0, from T.20.6 (Local Function) - the most accessible instantiation of this abstract tactic along this dimension.

equipment.rationale: Umbrella rating derived from this category's own children: the lowest-bar (easiest-for-attacker) equipment value found among them is Eq0, from T.20.5 (Denial of Service on Vehicle Function) - the most accessible instantiation of this abstract tactic along this dimension.

threats.name: Adversarial Machine Learning
threats.description: Using adversarial ML techniques to fool models by supplying deceptive input (e.g., altered stop signs) to cause vehicle perception systems to misclassify objects or respond inappropriately.

elapsedTime.rationale: Crafting physical adversarial inputs that survive real-world variables (lighting, angles) takes substantial time.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires deep understanding of neural networks and gradient exploitation.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: White-box attacks require access to training weights; black-box requires extensive model-behavior probing, both non-public.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires positioning the physical adversarial artifact within the target sensor's operational path, a moderately constrained condition.

equipment.rationale: Requires significant GPU compute for training the adversarial noise.

threats.notes: Same underlying Auto-ISAC ATM technique (ATM-T0005) as T.08.1 (Manipulate Environment), modeled independently here under the Affect Vehicle Function tactic with its own capability and feasibility profile.

threats.name: Analog Sensor Attacks
threats.description: Using analog sensor attacks to disrupt the availability of vehicle sensors (e.g., shining a laser into a Lidar receiver, transmitting ultrasonic noise).

elapsedTime.rationale: Shining a laser or emitting ultrasonic noise at a sensor produces an immediate disruptive effect.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Basic operation of a laser pointer or ultrasonic emitter requires no specialized expertise.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Basic physics of sensor blinding/jamming applies identically across OEMs, requiring no confidential knowledge.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires precise line-of-sight alignment with the target sensor during operation, a moderately constrained condition.

equipment.rationale: Commodity lasers or ultrasonic transducers are sufficient.

threats.notes: Same underlying Auto-ISAC ATM technique (ATM-T0004) as T.08.2 (Manipulate Environment), modeled independently here under the Affect Vehicle Function tactic with its own capability and feasibility profile.

threats.name: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Affecting Vehicle Function
threats.description: The adversary abuses standard diagnostic protocols to actuate vehicle functions, such as using UDS RoutineControl to actuate brakes or WriteMemoryByAddress to alter calibrations.

elapsedTime.rationale: Bypassing UDS SecurityAccess and issuing a RoutineControl actuation command takes days.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires bypassing UDS security boundaries.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires non-public knowledge of the specific ECU's diagnostic routine IDs and SecurityAccess scheme.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Diagnostic access is available whenever the bus/session is reachable, an easily obtainable window.

equipment.rationale: A commodity UDS diagnostic tool is sufficient.

threats.name: CAN Bus Denial of Service
threats.description: Flooding the CAN bus with high-priority messages (e.g., ID 0x000), preventing other ECUs from being able to communicate.

elapsedTime.rationale: Flooding high-priority frames begins immediately once bus access exists.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Simple scripts or off-the-shelf CAN tools generate bus floods with basic proficiency.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: CAN arbitration priority rules are a fully public part of the ISO 11898 standard.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Bus access, once obtained, provides a continuously available flooding window.

equipment.rationale: A commodity CAN interface capable of high-rate frame injection is sufficient.

threats.name: Denial of Service on Vehicle Function
threats.description: Performing DoS attacks to disrupt vehicle functionality by overwhelming an ECU with a high volume of requests or exploiting service vulnerabilities to cause a crash.

elapsedTime.rationale: Overwhelming a specific ECU service or exploiting a crash vulnerability takes days of testing.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Basic flooding/fuzzing scripts require only proficient-level skill.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Common request-handling and crash patterns are general software-engineering knowledge.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Once network/execution access exists, the target service is continuously attackable.

equipment.rationale: Standard scripting/flooding tools suffice.

threats.name: Local Function
threats.description: Using execution access on a targeted ECU to control the local hardware functions actuated directly by that device (e.g., executing code on a body controller to unlock doors).

elapsedTime.rationale: Calling the local actuator-control function once execution access exists is near-instantaneous.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires only basic familiarity with the ECU's local API/function calls.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Local hardware-control function calls are typically discoverable through firmware analysis of the compromised ECU itself.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Local actuator functions are continuously callable once execution access is held.

equipment.rationale: No special equipment beyond existing execution access is required.

threats.name: Modify Bus Message
threats.description: An adversary modifies or suppresses messages sent by another ECU on the internal network by winning arbitration or intercepting the bus logically/physically.

elapsedTime.rationale: Winning arbitration and reliably suppressing or modifying a specific target message takes days of bus analysis.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires intermediate protocol-timing expertise to win arbitration or interject reliably.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires knowledge of the target message's specific arbitration ID and timing, not publicly documented per-OEM.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Requires direct electrical access to the specific bus segment, a moderately constrained physical condition.

equipment.rationale: A commodity CAN/Ethernet interface with precise timing control is sufficient.

threats.name: Unintended Vehicle Network Message
threats.description: Sending unintended messages on the in-vehicle network (e.g., out of sequence, wrong rate, unauthorized parameters) post-escalation to trigger unauthorized physical functions.

elapsedTime.rationale: Sending an out-of-spec message once execution access exists is near-instantaneous.

specialistExpertise.rationale: Requires only basic scripting once execution access is held.

knowledgeOfTheItemOrComponent.rationale: Requires knowledge of the specific message IDs/parameters accepted by the target ECU, partially discoverable through observation.

windowOfOpportunity.rationale: Once execution access exists, message transmission is continuously available.

equipment.rationale: No special equipment beyond existing execution access is required.
